summary.headline: Kellton Tech Q2 FY27: revenue up about 6.5% YoY with EBITDA margin about 12.1%; dilution plans via rights and SCB issues still undecided.
summary.overview: Management reported Q2 FY27 revenue growth of about 6.5% YoY, EBITDA margin of about 12.1% and PAT margin of about 7.2%. The transcript is garbled in places, and the EPS comparison and prior-year base figures are not reliably stated. Management highlighted six client wins, including an AI-led claims automation platform, an automotive logistics IT infrastructure engagement, an agri-tech spin-off and a global hearing aid manufacturer's firmware R&D. The call was dominated by shareholder questions on a proposed rights issue and a preferential issue (SCBs), with no firm terms disclosed. Goodwill write-off treatment was also touched on briefly.

financial_highlights.value: figure garbled in transcript; comparison base stated as 5.97%

segments.name: segments
segments.commentary: The call gave no segment-level revenue or margin split; only a client-wins list was described, covering an AI-led insurance claims platform, automotive logistics IT infrastructure, an agri-tech spin-off (four or five applications and three back-end systems), a second agri-tech relationship, a top-five global hearing aid maker (firmware R&D), and one further win. Services versus product/IP is the only business split discussed, with no revenue figures attached.

guidance_outlook: No explicit revenue or margin guidance was given on the call.
Rights issue: awaiting NSE and BSE approvals; management expected to open the issue around end of current month or early next month. Promoter said to participate.
Preferential issue / SCB dilution: no size or valuation decided; management said it will be done when market conditions improve, to fund AI/IP investment.
capex_capacity: Board approved a fundraise (preferential issue) of up to about INR 50 million in September, per a shareholder's reading; proceeds to fund IP and AI product development (e.g., Phoenix AI and related platforms).

Goodwill: US goodwill written off; Indian goodwill (linked to Kumori acquisition) not yet written off due to differing Indian income-tax rules, but management said it will ultimately have to be written off.
demand_pricing: Six client wins in the quarter: (1) AI-driven enterprise claims platform for an insurer, covering submission, verification, review and settlement, integrated with provider network and policy administration; (2) premium automotive logistics provider, graduated from an audit to managing IT infrastructure support and maintenance; (3) agri-tech spin-off building four or five applications and three back-end systems for distribution and retailer chain; (4) a further agri-tech customer relationship; (5) a global top-five hearing aid manufacturer for engineering and firmware R&D; (6) one further win as described in the call.
Management said the company builds AI into core platforms ('AI ready') rather than adding it on top, positioning products for future AI use.
Management argued product/IP revenue earns higher valuation multiples than services, which is the rationale for IP-led strategy.

qa_highlights.question: How much valuation/dilution should be expected from the proposed SCB (preferential) issue of about INR 50 million?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no decision on size or valuation yet; dilution would occur when market and financial conditions improve, as they believe the stock is undervalued. Proceeds are for IP and AI products.

qa_highlights.question: Status of the rights issue approved by the board, and will the promoter participate?
qa_highlights.answer: Awaiting NSE and BSE approvals; expected to open around end of current or start of next month. The promoter will participate.

qa_highlights.question: What was the cost of the Kumori acquisition goodwill and how is it being treated?
qa_highlights.answer: US goodwill has been written off; Indian goodwill not yet written off because of different Indian tax rules, but it will ultimately have to be written off.

qa_highlights.question: Equity dilution from the SCB and rights issue combined?
qa_highlights.answer: No decision yet; management said services-based valuation is lower than product-based multiples, hence some dilution is needed. Line quality was poor, and the answer was repeated after reconnection.

risks_watch: Dilution from rights issue and SCB/preferential issue; final size, pricing and timing not disclosed.
Exchange approval timing for the rights issue (expected around end of current or early next month).
Goodwill write-off on the Kumori acquisition: Indian goodwill still on books and management says it will eventually be written off, a potential P&L hit.
Transcript quality is poor (muffled audio, garbled figures); reported EPS and several client and award details should be verified against the filed results and presentation.
Revenue growth of about 6.5% YoY is modest; no segment or geography split was provided.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the long-term AI/IP strategy and the value of the stock, but evasive on dilution size, pricing and timing. Chairman's audio was intermittently unclear, and the call was short with limited financial detail.
key_quotes: So it's AI ready, if they're not using it now, they will use it in future.
Selling the next copy is almost like zero cost, other than the marketing.

growth.why: No explicit revenue or margin guidance was given; Q2 FY27 revenue grew about 6.5% YoY, and six client wins were named without order values or timing, while the rights and SCB fundraise has no firm size or timing.
